question: In India, the ‘Aus’, ‘Aman’ and ‘Boro’ terms are associated with which crop from the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Paddy**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aus**, **Aman**, and **Boro** are terms associated with different varieties and cropping seasons of **Paddy** (rice) in India.
 
• **Aus** is sown in summer and harvested in autumn.
 
• **Aman** is sown in the monsoon season and harvested in winter.
 
• **Boro** is cultivated in the winter season and harvested in summer.
 
• These terms are specific to the traditional rice farming practices in regions like West Bengal and Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paddy** is a staple food crop in India, and it plays a crucial role in the country's agriculture and economy.
 
• India is one of the largest producers and consumers of rice in the world.
 
• Rice farming in India is highly dependent on the monsoon season, and the crop requires a lot of water for cultivation.
 
• The Green Revolution in India significantly boosted rice production, making the country self-sufficient in food grains.
 
• Modern techniques and high-yield varieties have also contributed to increased rice production in India.
